header: The "What to type" page of the user guide: for each feature of the search bar's tools, its NAME and the words that open it, with the alternatives separated by a front slash ("gold rate today / silver price / 22k gold"). This is one data file, read by src/components/help/QuickReferenceTab.tsx; I write nothing about a feature in the component. src/lib/help/quickReference.selftest.ts keeps the list honest: every string of every entry is run through the REAL detector (src/lib/tools/detect.ts) and must open the feature the entry says it opens, so a word that stops working, or a feature listed under a word that opens another, fails the tests. A string here is something the reader types AS IT IS; there is no blank to fill in. (The questions about people, hospital, circulars, announcements are on the Sample questions page: they are sentences, not words that open a tool.) My rule: EVERY feature is given its SHORT command (one or two words) and its LONG command (a phrase or a full question), or says in words why one of them does not exist (a value you type yourself, a command that needs all its words); the selftest checks that no feature is missing one of the two without saying so. `expect` is what the detector must answer for every string of the entry: the kind of line, and for a form or a live card its id, and for the news card the tab ("live:news:hi").

members.name: feature
doc: The feature's name, as the reader knows it.

members.name: short
doc: The SHORT commands: the fewest words that open it (one or two); I show each alternative with a "/" between

members.name: long
doc: The LONG commands: the same thing asked in full, in a phrase or a whole question; I show each alternative with a "/" between

members.name: noShort
doc: I show this on the page when there is no short command, and say why (a value you type yourself, or a command that needs all its words)

members.name: noLong
doc: I show this on the page when there is no long command, and say why.

members.name: what
doc: One short line: what opens, and anything worth knowing; words between ** ** are shown in bold

members.name: instant
doc: The result appears as you type (true), or the line needs the Enter key (false)

members.name: expect
doc: What the detector answers for each string (checked by the selftest); "records" is a question or a name that opens no tool but goes to the ordinary search of the intranet's own records

doc: Returns a line's pieces for the screen: the plain text and the bold text (written between ** **), in order; I leave an odd, unclosed ** as plain text.

behaviours: every string opens the feature its entry names (and nothing else)
the page is substantial: eight groups, more than forty features, more than a hundred and fifty commands
group ids are unique; every group and entry says what it covers; no string is empty or contains a slash (the slash is the separator on screen)
no string is listed under two features
a feature that opens a page is marked 'press Enter' and one that answers under the line is marked 'as you type', as the detector really behaves
every live card and every calculator form of the registry has an entry
every feature has a short command or says why it has none, and a long command or says why it has none (never silently missing)
a reason is given only where the command really does not exist (no feature has both a command and a 'none' note)
in the tools, a short command is one or two words and a long command is three or more (the records page is questions: judged by the person who asks)
the tool features that are not typed values have BOTH a short and a long command (only the values you type yourself, the reading of a marking and three words-only commands give a reason instead)
every kind is counted: the list has both short and long commands in every group
the records page covers the people, the hospital, PAX, holidays, circulars and circular questions, and says nothing of the deep search (EDS), which has its own tab
the filter finds a feature by its name, by a string or by a word of the note, and an empty text keeps all
the base switch's name is bold in the calculator entry: DEC · BIN · OCT · HEX is a bold piece, the words around it are plain, and no ** shows on the page
boldParts: plain text is one plain piece; an unclosed ** is left as it is; the search ignores the ** (typing 'hex switch' finds the calculator)
